question.prompt: The isosceles right triangle \(ABC\) has right angle at \(C\) and area \(12.5.\) The rays trisecting \(\angle ACB\) intersect \(AB\) at \(D\) and \(E.\) What is the area of \(\triangle CDE?\)

solutions.explanation:
The two outer triangles are congruent by symmetry, so finding one of their areas will determine the middle area. If the equal legs of \(ABC\) have length \(\ell>0\), then
\[
\frac{\ell^2}{2}=12.5,
\qquad \ell=5.
\]
The angles at \(A\) and \(B\) are each \(45^\circ\). We may take \(D\) to be the trisector intersection nearer \(A\), since exchanging \(D\) and \(E\) does not change the requested area. Then \(\angle ACD=30^\circ\).

Let \(F\) be the perpendicular foot from \(D\) onto \(CA\), and write \(DF=t>0\). The point \(F\) lies between \(C\) and \(A\). In right triangle \(CDF\), the side opposite the \(30^\circ\) angle is half the hypotenuse, so \(CD=2t\). The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
CF=\sqrt{(2t)^2-t^2}=\sqrt3\,t.
\]
Triangle \(AFD\) has a right angle at \(F\) and a \(45^\circ\) angle at \(A\), so \(AF=DF=t\). Adding the two parts of \(CA\) now gives
\[
5=CF+FA=(\sqrt3+1)t,
\qquad t=\frac{5(\sqrt3-1)}{2}.
\]
Triangle \(ACD\) has base \(CA=5\) and height \(t\), so its area is \(5t/2\). Reflection exchanging \(A\) and \(B\) also exchanges \(D\) and \(E\), so triangle \(BCE\) has the same area. Subtracting these two outer triangles leaves
\[
[ CDE ]=\frac{25}{2}-5t
=\boxed{\frac{50-25\sqrt3}{2}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Find and subtract the outer triangles
